AI Weekly Digest
July 07, 2026
A few things worth knowing this week — here's what's happening in AI, in plain English.
TL;DR — Top picks this week
If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
Google has changed its privacy settings so it can keep more of the data you upload—like photos, files, and audio or video recordings—to train its artificial‑intelligence services. This means any personal or work‑related content you store in Google could be used to improve the AI unless you opt out, which may raise privacy concerns for our team.
The only AI glossary you’ll need this year
A new reference guide lists the most common words and slang that have appeared as AI becomes more popular. It can help us all understand the terminology we hear in meetings, emails, or training about AI tools.
Top banking watchdogs issue stark warning over AI-driven cyber attacks
Bank regulators have issued a strong warning that criminals are now using artificial‑intelligence tools to launch cyber attacks against financial institutions. This matters to us because similar tactics could be directed at our banking partners or internal finance systems, increasing the need for strong security.
🛠️ Tools & Products
The only AI glossary you’ll need this year
A new reference guide lists the most common words and slang that have appeared as AI becomes more popular. It can help us all understand the terminology we hear in meetings, emails, or training about AI tools.
Read more →
The browser wars aren’t about search anymore — here are the best alternatives to Chrome and Safari
This article shares a list of web browsers that aim to compete with Chrome and Safari. Employees might consider trying one of these alternatives if they want different features, better privacy, or performance for their daily internet work.
Read more →
Money Magician – AI financial co-pilot for founders (not a budgeting app)
Money Magician is an artificial‑intelligence tool designed to act as a financial co‑pilot for company founders, not just a simple budgeting program. It could help our leadership get clearer insight into cash flow and make smarter financial decisions.
Read more →
🏢 Industry & Adoption
Microsoft is laying off 4,800 employees
Microsoft announced it will cut about 4,800 jobs, roughly 2 % of its staff, with most layoffs in its commercial sales and Xbox divisions. Changes at such a major software provider could influence the tools and services we rely on or affect market confidence.
Read more →
US investors will soon get access to SK Hynix, another memory maker riding the AI boom
South Korean chip maker SK Hynix, which makes memory products, is planning a large U.S. public stock offering driven by demand from artificial‑intelligence applications. The move highlights how AI is creating new investment opportunities and could impact the supply of hardware we use.
Read more →
Every major tech layoff in 2026 that has name-checked AI
This item is a list that tracks recent large tech company layoffs where AI was mentioned as a reason. It shows a pattern that AI may be influencing job cuts across the industry, which could affect how we think about staffing and skill needs.
Read more →
Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 employees across Xbox, commercial sales
Microsoft announced it is letting about 5,000 employees go, mainly from its Xbox and commercial sales teams, as part of a broader concern that AI is taking over some work. This signals that even big, well‑known companies are reducing staff in areas that may be similar to ours, so we should watch how AI might impact job security and roles here.
Read more →
🛡️ Safety & Policy
If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
Google has changed its privacy settings so it can keep more of the data you upload—like photos, files, and audio or video recordings—to train its artificial‑intelligence services. This means any personal or work‑related content you store in Google could be used to improve the AI unless you opt out, which may raise privacy concerns for our team.
Read more →
Top banking watchdogs issue stark warning over AI-driven cyber attacks
Bank regulators have issued a strong warning that criminals are now using artificial‑intelligence tools to launch cyber attacks against financial institutions. This matters to us because similar tactics could be directed at our banking partners or internal finance systems, increasing the need for strong security.
Read more →
AI coding assistant is quietly shipping your secrets
A recent report says that an AI‑powered coding assistant has been inadvertently sending out confidential information from users' projects. If our developers rely on such tools, this could expose proprietary code or business data.
Read more →
The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
The first known ransomware attack that used an AI agent handled the technical steps, but a person still chose the target, set up the infrastructure and provided stolen login details. This shows that AI can aid cyber criminals, so we need to stay vigilant about protecting our systems and credentials.
Read more →
Bank of England sees growing risks to financial stability from AI
The Bank of England has warned that artificial intelligence could create new risks that threaten the stability of the financial system. This could affect the regulatory landscape we operate in and may influence how we plan and manage our own finances.
Read more →

This means any personal or work‑related content you store in Google could be used to improve the AI unless you opt out, which may raise privacy concerns for our team.

  Read more: https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bank-england-sees-growing-risks-financial-stability-ai-2026-07-07/
